name: Stereo from mono: opposite filter frequencies plus inverse amplitude LFO
goal: Widen a mono synth path without Haas delay: split into L/R, offset parallel filter cutoffs in opposite directions (plus/minus frequency spread), then apply a unipolar LFO to left amplitude and its inverse (1−x) to right amplitude so levels see-saw in opposite phase — a modular stereo image that differs from Haas, mid/side EQ, and double-tracked asymmetric processing.

source.title: How to Make your Synthesizer Stereo

prerequisites: Mono synth voice (oscs → mixer → filters → amp is fine)
Ability to duplicate the post-filter (or post-amp) path into discrete L and R chains
LFO and simple arithmetic (invert / 1−x) or dual attenuators with opposite mod depth

inputs.name: spread_hz
inputs.description: How far L vs R filter cutoffs diverge

outputs.name: stereo_voice
outputs.description: L/R pair with spectral and amplitude differentiation

constraints: Portable modular/Web Audio recipe; not affiliated with any vendor.
Check mono fold-down — opposite filters and amplitude LFO can comb or pump when summed.

Distinct from haas-plus-phase-offset-width-automated (no inter-channel delay) and asymmetric-left-right-processing-width-mono-safe (no double-tracking/slap); complementary to midside-eq-bass-focus-width-depth for finishing.

steps.action: Start from a mono voice (tutorial: two simple waves + white noise → mixer → HP/LP → envelope). Confirm it is centered.

Frequency-spread stereo: put a filter (or filter pair) into a plus/minus or dual-cutoff mode and offset the cutoff so left and right emphasize different bands. This alone creates a static spectral stereo image.
steps.expect: L and R sound tonally different but still correlated

steps.action: Duplicate the signal into explicit left and right amplitude paths after the envelope (or duplicate the mixer into L/R).
steps.expect: Two gain stages feeding L and R outputs

steps.action: Create a unipolar LFO. Multiply the left path by the LFO. Build the right modulator as inverse unipolar: multiply LFO by −1 then add 1 (or use 1−x) so when left is loud, right is quiet and vice versa. Multiply the right path by that inverse.
steps.expect: Amplitude see-saw between L and R at the LFO rate

steps.action: Alternate simpler wiring: two attenuators on L and R modulated with opposite depths from the same LFO. Compare against the multiply version — both yield opposite-amplitude stereo.
steps.expect: Same widening effect with less patching

steps.action: Audition in stereo and mono. Reduce spread or LFO depth if mono pumps or hollows. Combine later with gentle M/S EQ if lows got too wide.
steps.expect: Wide in stereo; acceptable in mono

verification: With only filter spread: static width, no delay slap.
With inverse amp LFO: image rocks L↔R without changing pan knobs.
Mono sum remains usable at moderate depths.
